page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing the instance in the top 25% of evaluated hardware. However, multi-core scaling is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling within the average range. Memory bandwidth is stable, registering 1013.33 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 93.7 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Cryptographic and compression workloads perform consistently, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU encryption score of 17158.62 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 25.29 GB/sec.

The n2d-standard-16 offers a balanced resource profile for standard workloads, providing cost-efficient dedicated compute resources without the premium associated with memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated tiers. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning all storage operations must rely on network-attached persistent disks. This configuration is well-aligned with general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 13.61 GB/sec, database operations, and multi-threaded software compilation.
